ROEBUCK FOOD GROUP PLC

(“Roebuck”, “the Company” or “the Group”, AIM: RFG)

Proposed Placing and Subscription to raise up to €10 million

Capital Access Window

Roebuck Food Group plc ("Roebuck", “the Company” or “the Group") (AIM: RFG) is pleased to announce its intention to raise, in aggregate, up to €10 million by way of a placing and subscription of new ordinary shares at a price of 9 pence per share (“the Fundraise Price”) (“the Fundraising”).

Background

In February 2025 Roebuck completed a partial acquisition of 37.3% of GlasPort Bio (“GlasPort”), and of 16% of GlasPort Rumen Tech (“Rumen Tech”), (together “the 2025 Acquisition”).

GlasPort is an early-stage biotechnology company based in Galway, focused on Greenhouse Gas mitigation in agriculture, allowing farmers to increase their productivity and profitability whilst reducing their carbon emissions. GlasPort’s most developed technology is GasAbate ("GasAbate"). GasAbate is a market-ready manure management additive, proven to reduce methane emissions by 80%.

Rumen Tech’s chief product RumenGlas ("RumenGlas") is in an earlier stage of development. RumenGlas is a ruminant feed additive which has been shown to reduce methane, hydrogen and carbon dioxide emissions from ruminant livestock.

Since the 2025 Acquisition GlasPort continues to make encouraging operational and commercial progress as the business advances its strategy of building a leading verified platform for reducing the environmental footprint of livestock agriculture. GlasPort has continued to expand deployments across multiple European markets, strengthening its position with farmers, processors, industry stakeholders and regulators while steadily building the foundations for recurring revenue growth. Selected recent highlights include the following:

  • Leading Dairy Co-operative Validation

GlasPort has received confirmation that Arla, Europe's largest dairy co-operative, has approved GasAbate as a technology in the Arla FarmAhead Incentive programme from 2027 (“FarmAhead”). FarmAhead economically rewards milk producers for on-farm climate and environmental practices. FarmAhead, covers the seven European countries which make up their farmer-owner milk supply base; Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Luxembourg, Sweden, the Netherlands, and the UK. This development follows rigorous appraisal by Arla, including commercial on-farm pilots of the GasAbate technology, together with Compli360, its complementary measure, record and verify (MRV) system. GlasPort will now work with Arla to develop a roll-out strategy to provide Arla’s supplier farms with access to GasAbate as part of Arla's broader decarbonisation strategy.

  • Pilot Discussions with Other Large Processors

GlasPort is in discussions with  other leading European dairy processors regarding pilot installations on commercial dairy farms within their respective regions of operation. Whilst there is no certainty that any of these discussions will result in commercial sales of GasAbate, the Group is encouraged by the level of engagement with key participants across the European dairy industry.

  • Co-Benefits in Addition to Greenhouse Gas Reductions

GlasPort is exploring whether emerging data from pilot installations and GlasPort's ongoing research programmes are demonstrating a number of co-benefits beyond methane mitigation alone. Alongside lowering carbon footprint, the technology is showing potential to deliver wider benefits that may enhance GasAbate's value proposition for farmers, processors and regulators. Whilst further research will be conducted to measure and validate these potential co-benefits, our observations and preliminary research to date point to cost reductions (through better nutrient recycling and reduced need for purchased fertiliser, along with reduced agitation costs), efficiency gains ( through improved livestock performance in pigs housed over slurry storage tanks and  with improved crop yield from land fertilised with GasAbate-treated slurry) and environmental and farm-safety benefits (through reduced noxious and malodorous gas emissions from manure storage and handling).

Expanding Footprint: By December 2026, management expects GasAbate to be in use on over 90 farms, treating manure from 15,000 cows, across five European countries. GasAbate has also been rolled out on a large-scale integrated pig farm, with another such installation planned before year-end. Management expect these installs to generate annual recurring revenue of €1.15 million. A further 135 installs are expected for 2027.

More recently Roebuck has refocused its strategy exclusively around developing GlasPort and Rumen Tech. In light of this momentum and to ensure adequate capital availability to take advantage of these emerging market opportunities, Roebuck announces its intention to raise up to €10 million in new equity to fund the next stages of commercialisation and development of GlasPort and Rumen Tech respectively.

Potential Acquisitions of Other Shareholdings in GlasPort and Rumen Tech

As part of the 2025 Acquisition, Roebuck acquired a Call Option, (“the Call Option”) which would allow the Group, upon full exercise of this option, to increase its shareholding in GlasPort from 37.3% to 82.3% (pre management and staff growth-share dilution) on pre-agreed terms.

On 7 August 2026, this Call Option became exercisable, with the window to acquire part or all of these shares extending to February 2029. Under the disclosed terms of this Call Option, the price of the shares subject to the Call Option was set at the post-money value per share of the 2025 Acquisition, being €16.08 million, plus three additional increments based on achievement of three specific pre-agreed development milestones.

The first of these milestones was achieved in early 2025 (US Patent Approval) and a second is now achieved (Inclusion in a multinational food processor’s sustainability premia payment criteria), therefore increasing the equity value of GlasPort for the option exercise from €16.08 million to €25.08 million. The remaining milestone relates to inclusion in a country’s Greenhouse Gas Submission inventory calculation.  Settlement of all three developmental milestones during the Call Option window would increase the equity valuation of GlasPort, for the purposes of the Call Option exercise to €30.08 million.

Roebuck intends to exercise the Call Option and is in advanced discussions with those GlasPort shareholders, subject to the Call Option, with consideration to be settled entirely in Roebuck shares. Roebuck is also in discussions with the remaining shareholders of GlasPort (those not subject to the Call Option), to acquire their shares (excluding Growth Shares), with the consideration again being satisfied by the issue of Roebuck shares, (together “the GlasPort Acquisitions”).

In conjunction with these discussions, Roebuck is in discussion with the shareholders of Rumen Tech regarding acquisition of the 84% of shares (excluding Growth Shares) in that company not already owned by the Group, (“the Rumen Tech Acquisition”).

Whilst discussions regarding the GlasPort Acquisitions and the Rumen Tech Acquisition, (collectively “the Potential Acquisitions”) are at an advanced stage, there is no certainty that either will be completed at this time.

It is anticipated that the current Roebuck Long-Term Incentive Programme will be used for GlasPort and Rumen Tech employees, as part of the Potential Acquisitions.

Whiles exact terms have yet to be determined, the consideration for the Potential Acquisitions will result in the issuance of a significant amount of new Roebuck shares which will be dilutive to existing shareholders.

The Potential Acquisitions is separate to the proposed Fundraising and may be subject to separate shareholder approval, depending on the agreed terms when finalised.

Plant Based Ingredient Division

As part of the Group’s transformation, Roebuck has been progressing the divestment of Foro Food Solutions and Moorhead & McGavin (together “the Legacy Businesses”), to simplify the Group and focus its capital, management, resources and future growth strategy on GlasPort and Rumen Tech.

The Group is at an advanced stage in relation to the disposal of Foro Food Solutions.

The Legacy Businesses had net debt of £544,000 as at 30 October 2026, which is expected to be repaid in full following their divestment. Other debt-like items, include restructuring costs associated with the outgoing executive directors of £285,000, and obligations under the long-term lease of the Motherwell property.  It is anticipated that the net proceeds of the disposal of the Legacy Businesses will yield sufficient funds to cover the foregoing costs.

Placing and Subscription

The Company intends to raise gross proceeds of up to €10 million by means of:

  • a placing of new Ordinary Shares to certain institutional, professional, and other investors at the Fundraise Price (the “Placing”);
  • subscriptions for new Ordinary Shares from other investors at the Fundraise Price (the “Subscription”) (together, “the Fundraising”)

J&E Davy is acting as broker on the Placing. The Placing is to be conducted by way of the Book Build which will commence immediately following this Announcement and will be on the terms and conditions of the Placing Agreement described in Appendix 1 to this Announcement.

The Placing and Subscription will be subject to, inter alia the passing of certain resolutions, authorising the issue of the Placing Shares and Subscription Shares at an Extraordinary General Meeting of Roebuck (“EGM”) to be convened following completion of the Book Build. A circular to shareholders containing the proposed resolutions to be proposed at the EGM and other information will be despatched as soon as possible after the Fundraising.

The Company has decided to utilise a Capital Access Window in connection with the Fundraising. The Capital Access Window facility provides the Company with a voluntary mechanism to implement a temporary pause in the trading of its shares on AIM to facilitate reaching a broader range of investors, and to provide pricing stability during the Fundraising.

Accordingly, trading in the Ordinary Shares of the Company will be suspended with effect from 7.30 a.m. on 2 November 2026. In the coming days, theCompany expects to issue a further announcement detailing the results of the Fundraising and that trading in the Ordinary Shares will resume. The Fundraise Price represents a discount of approximately 56.1 per cent. to the closing mid-market price of 20.5 pence per Ordinary Share on 30 October 2026, being the last practicable date prior to the Company entering into the Capital Access Window.

Use of Proceeds

It is the Board’s intention that the net proceeds of the Fundraising will be applied to support the development and growth of GlasPort and Rumen Tech and will not be used to fund or discharge any legacy costs or liabilities associated with existing non-core activities of Roebuck.

The Fundraising (net of expenses of the Fundraising and Potential Acquisitions) will be deployed in both GlasPort and Rumen Tech in the following areas:

  • Working capital: Funding operations and cash-flow needs as GlasPort scales.
  • Commercial deployment: Accelerating rollout through farm installations, and processor-led programmes across beef, pig and duck sectors.
  • Research & Development: Expanding GlasPort’s value proposition through ammonia reduction, dosage optimisation and validation of wider animal, environmental and economic benefits.
  • Compli360 optimisation: Developing lower-cost, faster installation and Internet of Things architecture for scalable farm deployment.
  • Team expansion: Strengthening commercial, technical, operational, regulatory, engineering and data capabilities to support European growth.
  • International partnerships: Establishing processor, co-operative and distributor partnerships across targeted European dairy and pig markets. 
  • Rumen Tech development: Advancing the development of the Rumen Tech feed additive.
  • Ownership simplification: A small minority of the proceeds may be used to support the simplification of the ownership structures of GlasPort and Rumen Tech, through the acquisition of shares from certain minority shareholders, should suitable opportunities arise.

Following completion of the Fundraising, Roebuck intends to provide GlasPort with an initial unsecured loan of €1 million (“the Loan”) prior to completion of the Potential Acquisitions set out above, funds from which may be advanced to Rumen Tech with Company consent. The Loan will  have an interest rate of 2% per annum above ECB base rate, payable annually in arrears. The Loan will have a one year term, thereafter subject to repayment on one year’s notice, subject to accelerated repayment in the case of an insolvency event in any of the Company, GlasPort or Rumen Tech.The remainder of the Fundraising will be deployed post completion of the Potential Acquisitions. If the Potential Acquisitions for any reason do not complete, Roebuck will explore other methods of investing the proceeds into GlasPort Bio and Rumen Tech. Failing this, the remaining funds will be returned to shareholders.

The entry into the Loan will constitute a related party transaction for the purposes of Rule 13 of the AIM Rules for Companies. The Directors of the Company consider, having consulted with the Company’s Nominated Adviser, Davy, that the terms of the Loan are fair and reasonable insofar as the shareholders of the Company are concerned.

Management and Governance Changes

As previously announced, Mr. Justin McCarthy, assumed the role of CEO of Roebuck, today 31 October 2026, and joined the board. He has maintained his roles as CEO of GlasPort and Executive Chairman of Rumen Tech.

Mr. Padraic Lenehan, who was recently appointed as CFO of GlasPort, will become CFO of Roebuck and join the board from completion of the Fundraising, replacing Mr. Aidan Hughes who will depart the Company and the Board at that time. Mr. Lenehan is an experienced finance executive with more than two decades of experience in the agri-food sector, having formerly served as Finance Director and Company Secretary of Donegal Investment Group plc. These executive appointments will further streamline group management structures and reduce operating costs.

In addition, Roebuck is pleased to announce that Mr. Padraic McManus will join the board of Roebuck on completion of the Fundraising and will take over the responsibilities of Non-executive Chairman. Mr McManus is former Chief Executive of ESB, Chairman of Eir and Chairman of the Greenlink Interconnector Project.  He has extensive senior leadership and board experience. He was Chairman and President of the Council of ESRI and also held senior board and advisory positions across a range of Irish operations

Further Information

Commenting on the Fundraising, Non-Executive Chairman Tommy Conway stated: “Since our initial investment in GlasPort in February 2025, the businesses have made tremendous progress in creating market awareness across key target markets, developing an effective MRV system to complement GasAbate, building a strong commercial team and rolling out installations on large-scale farms in five European countries. Considering these early achievements, I believe that our investment in GlasPort has been significantly de-risked, and GlasPort is on a clear path to developing recurring income streams and commercialisation across various farm enterprises in several large European markets. Furthermore, I believe that now is the right time to simplify and streamline Roebuck's operations and governance, while strengthening the balance sheet to support the rapid scale-up of GlasPort's market-leading solutions. I want to take this opportunity to thank the outgoing executives, Kieran Mahon and Aidan Hughes, for their significant contributions over many years to Roebuck, and its predecessor, Norish plc. I also wish to note their unstinting support throughout the current transaction process, and the assistance they have given to the incoming executive directors.  On behalf of Roebuck, I want to welcome Justin McCathy as CEO and director, and Padraic Lenehan as CFO Designate. Justin and Padraic both bring a wealth of experience and strong commercial track-records in agribusiness to the Group. Finally, I want to welcome Padraig McManus who will join the Board as Non-executive Chairman on completion of the fundraise. On behalf of Roebuck shareholders, I wish Justin, Padraic and Padraig every success in their new roles.

data.title: Wall Street slides as AI cash burn worries spark tech selloff
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes down: Dow 1.08%, S&P 500 2.08%, Nasdaq 3.37%
  • Intel slides after reporting big cash burn
  • Crypto firms slide after reports that hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance

By Stephen Culp and Purvi Agarwal

US stocks tumbled on Friday, with the Nasdaq plunging to a three-month low following disappointing quarterly results from Intel and Amazon, which amplified growing fears surrounding AI-related companies' massive spending on the nascent technology, and concerns about when or whether the cash burn will start to pay off.

All three major US stock indexes slumped, with the Nasdaq sliding 3.4%. The tech-heavy index has dropped more than 8% from its all-time closing high reached on October 6.

The tech rout was sparked by disappointing quarterly results from Intel and Amazon released late on Thursday. The companies' shares slumped 2.1% and 30.9%, respectively.

Chip stocks veered sharply lower, with Nvidia down 5.3% and AMD sliding 12.1%. The broader chips index shed 8.7% and was headed for a monthly loss. Server makers Dell and HP lost 12.5% and 10.8%, respectively.

Amazon and Intel were set to wipe out nearly $200 billion in combined market value if losses hold, setting up the Nasdaq-100 to erase over $1 trillion on Friday.

"It's fair to say that this week, not just today, has been very much about the future of AI and what that's going to look like, whether there will be a positive return on investment and if so, how quickly," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors in New York.

"Companies that are performing and meeting the very lofty expectations that have been set are doing well," Pursche added. "Those that are falling short and seem to be missing the mark or not executing as expected are getting punished."

The selloff put all three indexes on course to close lower on the week. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq are on track to log monthly losses, while the Dow appears set to end October with a gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 566.81 points, or 1.08%, to 51,778.86, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 160.54 points, or 2.08%, to 7,559.85 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 881.35 points, or 3.37%, to 25,303.37.

The S&P 500 tech sector was on track for its largest monthly percentage loss since March 2025, and communication services looked to be headed for its biggest monthly drop since April 2022.

Third-quarter earnings season has passed the halfway mark, with 299 companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 82% have beaten consensus expectations, according to LSEG data.

Analysts now expect third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.6%, year-on-year, per LSEG.

Oil supermajors Exxon Mobil and Chevron both beat quarterly profit expectations, benefiting from soaring profit margins as a result of energy supply disruptions arising from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia's war in Ukraine. The stocks gained 1.7% and 1.4%, respectively.

Starbucks slid 1.4% after the coffee chain forecast an annual revenue decline due to its divestiture of its Chinese business.

Cryptocurrency-related firms Coinbase , Strategy , and Robinhood fell between 8.8% and 13.6% in the wake of reports that hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.8-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange. There were 147 new highs and 298 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,144 stocks rose and 3,559 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.11-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 43 new 52-week highs and five new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 62 new highs and 290 new lows.

data.title: Swiss Market Ends Modestly Higher
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - The Switzerland market's benchmark SMI ended modestly higher on Friday after holding firm throughout the trading session, outperforming most of its peers in Europe.

Investors continued to react to the latest quarterly earnings announcements, while keeping an eye on global economic data and recent policy moves of major central banks.

The SMI ended with a gain of 53.80 points or 0.36% at 14,810.66, after moving between 14,777.23 and 14,849.75.

Nestle moved up 2.3% and Lindt & Spruengli gained about 2.2%. Swiss RE, Galderma Group and Swisscom climbed 1.6%-1.7%. Givaudan gained nearly 1.5%.

Novartis, Straumann Holding and Schindler Ps gained 1%-1.1%. Richemont, Sonova, Zurich Insurance, Alcon, Helvetia Baloise Holding, Lonza Group, Sika and Roche ended up by 0.4%-0.85%.

VAT Group ended lower by 5%. Logitech International dropped 4.15% and ABB drifted down by 3.3%.

Holcim, Sandoz Group, UBS Group, Julius Baer, Amrize and Partners Group settled lower by 0.5%-1.3%.

In economic news, a report from Swiss Economic Institute showed Switzerland's KOF Economic Barometer fell to 107.6 in October, down from 109.1 in September and below market expectations of 108.3. Despite the decline, the barometer remained above its medium-term average, indicating a continued robust outlook for the Swiss economy.

data.title: Record Pace of Eaton Fire Claims for SCE Program Continues Ahead of Nov. 30 Deadline
data.description:
October saw the highest number of claims submitted this year to Southern California Edison’s Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program, as community members directly impacted by the Eaton Fire continue to evaluate their options for seeking compensation ahead of the Nov. 30, 2026, claim submission deadline. The record month builds on increasing claim activity in recent months. More than 41% of claims have now been submitted through an attorney or authorized representative.

“It’s encouraging to see more families and businesses turning to the program as they recover and move forward,” said Pedro J. Pizarro, president and CEO of Edison International, SCE’s parent company. “There is still time to submit a claim before the November 30 deadline, and we encourage eligible community members to explore what compensation may be available to them.”

The program is designed to provide compensation in line with settlement values for similar claims in past wildfire lawsuits through a more streamlined approach. As of Oct. 30, 2026:

  • More than 5,550 claims submitted, consisting of nearly 17,000 individuals, trusts and legal entities, with 41% submitted by attorneys or authorized representatives.
  • More than 3,200 offers extended to over 8,000 claimants, totaling about $1.1 billion. Nearly 80% of offers have been accepted, with more pending. Only about 2% of offers have been declined.
  • More than 4,450 claimants paid, totaling over $625 million, with many more in process.

Get The Facts

It is important that eligible community members make fully informed decisions based on accurate facts. For anyone who has been told that waiting for the first trial date will provide compensation on a similar timeline or within months of the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program deadline, that is false. Resolution through litigation will be lengthy. Only eight households have been selected by the court to participate in the initial trial.

Participation in the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program results in a timely, no-commitment offer and still keeps the option open to pursue the longer litigation path if desired. Claims submitted by Nov. 30 will continue to be reviewed and processed afterward, even if validation or preparation of an offer has not been completed. Submitting a claim, receiving an offer and evaluating that offer do not waive a claimant’s rights.

More Represented Claimants Turning to the Program

Claimants represented by attorneys are increasingly participating in the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program. For claimants represented at the time they submit a claim, offers include an additional 20% of the net damages portion to help address legal expenses.

Angela Loera, who lost her home in the Eaton Fire, is among those who participated in the program with the assistance of an attorney. Her attorney, Derek Whitefield, has helped hundreds of claimants navigate the program.

“Thank you for making this process easy, quick and seamless,” said Loera in a handwritten note shared with SCE.

Fair Offers, Fast Payments

Litigation may take years. Some claims arising from 2017 and 2018 fires remain pending today. The Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program offers a more streamlined alternative, with offers and payments measured in weeks or months rather than years. To keep this option available, claims must be submitted by Nov. 30, 2026, and claimants must remain responsive to requests for information and communications related to their claim.

  • On average, offers are being delivered within 36 days following submission of a substantially complete claim.
  • Payments are made within 30 days after all conditions in the settlement agreement have been satisfied, with many claimants receiving payment in as little as two to three weeks.

Learn More and Get Help Starting a Claim

SCE will host in-person and virtual sessions where community members can learn about the program, ask questions and receive help starting a claim. Register here for the following sessions:

  • Thursday, Nov. 12, 6 p.m. (Westminster Presbyterian Church, 1757 N. Lake Ave., Pasadena)
  • Thursday, Nov. 19, 6 p.m. (virtual)

To submit a claim and access detailed guidance in English and Spanish, visit the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program web page. One-on-one assistance is available in multiple languages by phone or in person, from start to finish. Call 888-912-8528 to get started.

About Southern California Edison

An Edison International () company, Southern California Edison is one of the nation’s largest electric utilities, serving a population of approximately 15 million via 5 million customer accounts in a 50,000-square-mile service area within Central, Coastal and Southern California.

Roebuck Food Group plc (AIM: RFG), a group focused on growth and innovation within the food and agribusiness sectors, is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr Justin Gerard McCarthy as Chief Executive Officer and as an executive director of the Company, effective tomorrow 31 October 2026.

As announced in the Company’s interim results on 30 September 2026, Mr McCarthy succeeds Kieran Mahon following the refocusing of the Group’s business on its investments in Glasport Bio Limited (“GlasPort”) and Glasport Rumen Tech Limited (“Rumen Tech”).

Mr McCarthy (49) is currently Chief Executive Officer of GlasPort and Executive Chairman of Rumen Tech, roles he will retain following his appointment as CEO of Roebuck. Both businesses develop technologies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions from livestock production. He has experience across the agricultural sector, having worked with ABP Food Group, Dawn Meats and Teagasc, and previously served as CEO of the Irish Farmers Journal Group. He brings a combination of leadership, commercial insight and knowledge of agriculture and the global food sector. Mr McCarthy is a graduate in Agricultural Science from Harper Adams University and has also undertaken executive education at Harvard and University College Dublin’s Michael Smurfit Graduate Business School.

data.title: Delhivery Q2 Results: Revenue crosses ₹3,000 crore for first time; EBITDA nearly triples
data.description:
Delhivery Ltd on Friday (October 30) reported its first-ever quarterly revenue of over ₹3,000 crore, with revenue from services rising 20% year-on-year to ₹3,066 crore in the second quarter of FY27.

EBITDA nearly tripled year-on-year to ₹205 crore, with a margin of 6.7%, while consolidated net profit stood at ₹41 crore, or a margin of 1.3%.

The company's express parcel business handled 325 million shipments during the quarter, up 32% year-on-year, while revenue from the segment grew 22%. Part Truck Load (PTL) volumes rose 14% to 545,000 metric tonnes (MT), with revenue increasing 23% year-on-year.

Delhivery ended the September quarter with a cash balance of ₹4,676 crore.

The company said its profitability improved sequentially despite an inflationary cost environment. It also reported its best network service levels ahead of the festive season, despite rising fuel prices, labour availability issues and multiple statutory changes.

Delhivery said it continues to invest in technology to improve demand shaping, infrastructure productivity, reduce dependence on labour in under-the-roof operations and simplify customer experience.

The company said its early investments in artificial intelligence (AI) are beginning to deliver results through improved sales productivity and customer onboarding, faster resolution of claims and disputes, and fraud detection.

Delhivery Robotics, its in-house automation lab, has started production of customised autonomous vehicles for in-facility movement operations. The company has also begun testing robotics systems across under-the-roof operations in partnership with global leaders in the physical AI domain.

Delhivery said the improvements in network service levels and profitability provide momentum heading into the second half of FY27.

The company serves over 59,000 clients across e-commerce and express parcel transportation, PTL and full truckload (FTL) freight, warehousing and supply chain solutions, international freight, intra-city on-demand logistics, data solutions and software-as-a-service offerings, including AI-powered mapping APIs and warehouse and transportation management systems.

data.title: Caterpillar, Deere on Different Roads With Investors Lately — WSJ
data.description:
By Bob Tita

Caterpillar's strong generator business with AI data centers made it the envy of the machinery industry over the last year as the company's shares soared with high-flying tech stocks.

But decent third-quarter sales and profit from the construction and mining equipment maker on Thursday were brushed aside by jittery investors. The company's shares dropped more than 9% Thursday in a sell-off of stocks with exposure to the AI sector. Caterpillar, which has fallen more than 20% in the past month, was down about 4% Friday.

Rival machinery manufacturer Deere, which ironically has for years tried to attract more tech-focused investors with its automated farming software, has avoided the AI carnage. Deere's shares are up about 45% since the start of the year. Investors have piled into Deere on the expectation that a long slump in the U.S. farm equipment market will ease next year and farmers will start buying more Deere tractors again.

Deere is up about 1.5% on Friday.

data.title: Fed Needs to Implement at Least Two More Rate Increases, Dallas Fed's Logan Says — Update
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

The Federal Reserve needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases given the current economic outlook after the central bank voted to hold interest rates steady this week, according to Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan.

Without any monetary-policy restraint, inflation will continue to trend above target unless unexpected shocks occur, Logan said at an event in Davidson, N.C., on Friday.

"It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases," Logan said. "After that, it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate," she added.

There had been speculation that Logan would dissent at October's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, given her previous calls for tighter monetary policy and a previous dissent she gave in July. On Friday, she offered more explanation to why she instead supported the committee's decision to hold interest rates where they are.

Financial markets have been volatile in response to news on the technology-investment outlook and geopolitical developments, she said. In such an environment, adjusting policy more gradually can help households, businesses and market participants adapt to higher rates and reduce the risk that economic activity deteriorates more sharply than necessary, she added.

Moreover, Logan said the precise timing of each rate increase has little effect on the longer-term rates most borrowers pay as long as market participants understand the FOMC's policy plans.

In addition, skipping a meeting of rate increases doesn't change the monetary-policy destination, Logan argued.

"By making the destination clear, the FOMC can better help the economy adapt and obtain the promised benefits of a skip," she explained.

Given the current outlook, the end goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive to sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices, Logan said.

data.title: Bank of Canada Must Rethink Further Rate Hikes Amid 'Squishy-Soft' Data — Market Talk
data.description: Days after raising its policy rate by a quarter point, the Bank of Canada faces a reality check over its outlook for accelerating growth, says David Rosenberg, head of market-strategy firm Rosenberg Research. Data covering non-farm payrolls indicate a 49,600 decline in jobs in August. Further, GDP stalled in August, and is expected to contract in September--leading to annualized growth of 1.3% in 3Q, or well below the BOC's 2% forecast. "Can the central bank really ignore the economy and this recent squishy-soft set of economic data?," says Rosenberg about pending rate hikes. He argues BOC based its rate-hike decision on "dubious surveys instead of facts on the ground," adding there is no evidence of elevated fuel prices spilling over to non-energy goods. data.title: AMD Stocks Drop 11% With a $13 Billion Revenue Test Approaching
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices , the processor and AI-accelerator designer, has a bigger hurdle than winning server business: turning that growth into profit. Shares fell 11.01% to $504.05 at 12:45 p.m. ET on October 30, ahead of its November 3 earnings report. Susquehanna raised its price target from $620 to $650 and maintained Buy, pointing to data-center opportunities while flagging margin pressure from the GPU ramp. That leaves investors weighing a bigger sales opportunity against the cost of delivering it.

The numbers give that debate a clear test. AMD's August outlook called for September-quarter revenue of $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, with adjusted gross margin near 56%. The revenue midpoint implies roughly 12.7% growth from the June quarter's $11.536 billion. More revenue could strengthen the AI story, but holding margins while expanding GPU deliveries would provide firmer evidence that the opportunity is translating into profitable growth.

GuruFocus' snapshot captures the tension: an 82/100 GF Score, strong growth and financial-strength readings, but a weak GF Value reading. At 129.34 times earnings and 12.24 times book value, the valuation appears to leave limited room for disappointment even after the sharp decline. Susquehanna's roughly 4.8% target increase adds optimism; November's results must supply the evidence. Revenue delivery, gross margin and the next outlook could determine whether AMD's expanding data-center business can support those expectations.
